name: ZOLE
description: Zole (Zolīte) is Latvia's national card game. 3 players (4-5 with dealer out). 26-card deck. 8 each + 2-card talon. Permanent trumps: Queens > Jacks > Diamonds. Declarer: take talon, discard 2, win 61+ of 120 card points. Solo = no talon. Mazais = lose every trick. Table game = fewest points.

content.text: Zole (Zolīte) is Latvia's national card game. 3 players (4-5 with dealer out). 26-card deck. 8 each + 2-card talon. Permanent trumps: Queens > Jacks > Diamonds. Declarer: take talon, discard 2, win 61+ of 120 card points. Solo = no talon. Mazais = lose every trick. Table game = fewest points.

Zole is a Latvian point-trick game derived from the German game Schafkopf, belonging to the ace-ten family in which jacks and queens are permanent trumps. It became Latvia's national card game. The name comes from the Latvian word zole (sole). Official rules and terminology were published by the Latvian Zole Game Federation (LZSF) in 1996. The game is deeply embedded in Latvian culture and is commonly played for money.

items.text: Four players: Dealer receives no cards and sits out. Some play dealer pays or receives same as opponents; others play dealer has no part in scoring.
Small Solo (Mazā zole): Bid outranks Ordinary Solo; declarer undertakes to lose every trick. Talon unused. If successful declarer receives 6 stakes from each opponent; if not pays 7 each.

Pools: When all pass, no play; one collective pool token placed, cards thrown in. When declarer loses and pools exist, one personal pool before declarer. When declarer wins, one pool removed (personal first, then collective, then opponent personal).
